Thanks for the time today, Alex — really helpful to walk through your architecture and compliance priorities. Per our call, I wanted to recap the Data Handling & Compliance milestone for the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and confirm next steps so we can keep to your target close window.

High-level goal (what HealthSync needs):
- Ensure Redwood’s hosted inference for PHI-bearing data meets retention, logging, and audit trail requirements, and that we can sign a BAA.

Proposed MAP milestone: Data handling & compliance (owner, target date, dependencies)
1) BAA review and signature — Owner: HealthSync Legal + Redwood Legal (me/Marcus) — Target: 2026-03-22
2) SOC2 evidence & technical appendix delivery — Owner: Redwood Security (Marcus to supply artifacts) — Target: 2026-03-10
3) Data retention policy alignment (retention window, deletion APIs) — Owner: HealthSync Product + Redwood PM — Target: 2026-03-18
4) Audit logging and access controls confirmation (log retention, log export) — Owner: Redwood SRE/Security (Marcus) — Target: 2026-03-18
5) Final compliance sign-off (security + legal) — Owner: HealthSync + Redwood — Target close: 2026-04-15

Dependencies called out on the call:
- Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II report and a technical appendix describing logging, KMS, and key management flow (Marcus to attach).
- HealthSync to surface any additional PHI handling constraints (specific retention windows / regional data residency) and any custom audit requirements.
- Legal review for BAA and any HIPAA-specific addenda.

Action items for this thread:
- Marcus: please attach SOC2 + a short one-pager on KMS/logging (by EOD 03/05)
- Alex: confirm BAA review owner on your side and any special retention windows (by 03/08)
- I’ll draft the MAP PDF and circulate for signature after we have the artifacts and confirmed owners.

Attaching a draft MAP skeleton in the next email. Let me know if I missed anything from the call.

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side:
- BAA: legal owner is me (I'll shepherd internally) but security will need to review the technical appendix. I'll confirm with Legal and loop in our counsel by 03/08.
- Retention: we have two retention windows — 30 days (short-term analytics) and up to 7 years for records tied to billing/claims. We need confirmation that Redwood can support configurable retention and a programmatic delete API.
- PHI handling: most data is PHI. HIPAA coverage is mandatory, and we'd like explicit statements about PHI in the BAA and any flow diagrams showing encryption-at-rest + key ownership.

Please have Marcus include any KMS key ownership language and clarify whether Redwood offers a customer-managed-key option in private deployments vs hosted. Also, is there a way to export audit logs to our Splunk instance?

If we can get the SOC2 and a KMS/logging appendix by 03/05, we can accelerate review.

Hi Alex / Marissa — attaching the MAP draft (HealthSync-MAP-draft-v1.pdf) and the SOC2 Type II report (redacted, SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf). Also included a short KMS & logging appendix (redwood_kms_architecture.png) that shows:
- Encryption at rest: AES-256, keys stored in customer-dedicated KMS namespaces for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers use Redwood KMS with HSM-backed keys and optional CMK (customer-managed key) integration via AWS KMS or GCP KMS.
- Audit logs: request & admin audit trails are retained for 365 days by default for hosted; can be extended for Dedicated/Private. Logs can be streamed to customer Splunk/Datadog via secure syslog or S3 sink (we'll provide a small ingestion playbook).
- Delete API: we expose a programmatic data purge endpoint and also a retention policy configuration per dataset (we'll include API examples in the appendix).

Regarding PHI: Redwood is prepared to sign a BAA; legal will need to review standard language. For hosted deployments, customer data is logically separated and encrypted; we recommend Dedicated or Private if HealthSync needs strict tenant-dedicated KMS and longer log retention.
